reader_question: What do I need to do before moving, and when?
demand_source: dataforseo volume/KD via scripts/lib/keyword_data.py (KEYWORD_PROVIDERS=dataforseo); DataForSEO SERP reads reports/mindmap-pass/2026-10-26-moving/serp.json
decision_gap: Page one for 'moving checklist' is mover-company blogs, realtor posts, consumeraffairs and hgtv with static lists or PDFs; none filters tasks by rent/own at each end, distance, mover type, season or location (SERP sample of 10 results, not a claim about every competitor). 'Moving to another state checklist' is owned by Reddit threads.
method: calculated + reported: one rule per item in src/lib/checklists.ts (MOVING) drawn from cited federal guidance (USPS, USA.gov, IRS, FMCSA, Vote.gov, NFPA, ready.gov, HUD); scenario counts produced by running those rules

findings.label: calculated
findings.text: scenario item counts per counts.json (library 88; A 46, B 63, C 49)

findings.label: reported
findings.text: federal rules listed in the row prompt's CLOSED FACT LIST; FMCSA pages read 2026-10-26

counterexample: A reader moving between two states whose climates differ gets climate items for the state they choose only; the switches are a starting point and they can turn on conditions for either home.
exclusions: No state-specific deadlines (license, registration, deposit return, notice periods), no mover or truck prices, no cost estimates.
unknowns: Which items readers use; whether customization changes rankings.
would_change: A change to FMCSA's released-value or claim-filing rules, the IRS moving-expense rule, or a reader-reported missing task.
selected_medium: interactive tool + server-rendered full list (tool is client-only)

provenance.scopeAndLimits: Counts are rule outputs for example moves, not user data or product tests.
provenance.publicMethod: workedExample section + 'How the checklist is built' + the full list with Only-if tags
